There is a man in London who has been matching people's eyes in glass for 27 years. His father made glass eyes - his grandfather and he received the ordinary training of an artist in order to be able to blend and mix colours as by second nature. He made eyes for famous actresses and well known princess among others. He made an eye for the late Gen. Booth when he was 81. These glass eyes can hardly be distinguished from the true eye. He puts a small bulge on the back of the glass eyes in such a position that the muscles of the eyesocket move the artificial thing in unison with the movements of the good eye. Then he makes eyes with dilating pupils (the pupil is the dark circle right in the centre of the eye). That is the say in daylight the pupil is small; in artificial light it enlarges as do the pupils of all our eyes. He canmatch your eye in glass in half an hour while you sit beside him for pattern. He sits at a bench in his workshop in the centre of London with an array of glass tubes and glass rods of varying colours and thicknesses and a glass blower's burner before him - the flame of which can be varied according to the degree of heat he needs. He blows a bubble of opal glass the size of an eyeball first; then while the tip is still red he puts on the ground colour of the iris (the ring round the pupil) by heating am joining to the red tip tiny streams of molten blue glass or brown glass. Now he heats the end of a rod of black or nearly black glass and joint the spot of that on to the centre of the iris. This is the pupil. At the time the bubble - still on the tube from which it was drawn and blown - is turning deftly in his fingers so that the eye seems to grow of itself. The lens comes next a coating of crystal glass from a thick rod which gradually spreads over the face of crystal glass from a thick rod which gradually spreads over the face of the opal bulb and becomes part of it. He made eyes for well known a stresses and Princesss among others, and also made an eye for the late General Booth when he was 81. These glass eyes can hardly be distinguished from the true eyes. He puts a bulge on the back of the glass eye in such a position that the muscles of the gum eye socket move the glass artificial thing in unison with the movements of the good eyes.
